name: Republic of Cospaia (1440–1826)
description: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly to the lower hoist, black above and white below.
history: Cospaia, a village left out of the boundary between the Papal States and Florence in 1440, remained an unintended free republic for nearly four centuries until it was partitioned on 26 June 1826. The black-and-white flag is recorded by Roberto Breschi; the republic's motto was 'Perpetua et firma libertas'.
